turns.text: Add a warm, clear English voice-over to the attached silent clip, saying exactly: “Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.” Keep the video unchanged. No music or captions. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**No generation has run, and no generation credits have been spent.**

Your request needs two steps: synthesize the exact script as English speech, then add that audio track without changing the video. **The connected Magic Hour tools don’t provide a standalone text-to-speech tool or an audio-only merge tool**, so I can’t complete this faithfully—or quote a valid Magic Hour cost for it. Lip-sync and video-generation tools would change the visuals, so I won’t use those.

**The cheapest option is a free local workflow:**
- Record the script yourself, or use a free text-to-speech voice with a warm, clear delivery.
- Add it to the clip using a free editor or FFmpeg. With FFmpeg, the video stream can be copied unchanged while the narration is added.
- **Magic Hour cost: 0 credits.** External voice-service costs, if any, depend on that service.

Your exact 22-word script should take roughly **9–11 seconds** at a clear pace. I haven’t inspected the clip’s duration, so I can’t confirm it fits.

**Shorter or smaller?** Keeping the exact wording leaves limited room to shorten the narration without rushing. Lowering the video resolution isn’t needed for an audio-only merge and would violate “keep the video unchanged.” A compressed narration track adds very little file size.

If you can supply a recorded voice-over, I can give you the exact FFmpeg command to add it without altering the video—no music or captions.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **0 Magic Hour credits**: record the narration yourself and merge it locally. I can’t record speech or perform that merge through the connected tools, so nothing has run.

Record this exactly, warmly and clearly:

> Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

Save it as `voiceover.wav`, then run this free FFmpeg command in the folder containing both files:

```bash
ffmpeg -i talk-one-silent.mp4 -i voiceover.wav \
  -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 \
  -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 128k \
  -af apad -shortest \
  talk-one-with-voiceover.mp4
```

This copies the video stream **unchanged**, adds only your narration, and preserves the clip’s duration. Make sure the recording fits within the clip; otherwise the narration will be cut off. No music or captions are added.
